checks.evidence: No comparison yet against published Site01/Site04 illumination (e.g. Barker et al. 2021, Mazarico et al. 2011).

Bound 1.76e-05 deg (~0.534 m) from NAIF generic_kernels/fk/satellites/moon_de440_220930.tf: "DE440 vs DE421 mean Earth frame difference" (max rotation 2000-2040 = 3.0709840342771E-07 rad, ~53.4 cm on the surface). Smallest |margin|: Sun 0.02995 deg, Earth 0.01257 deg; samples that could flip: Sun 0, Earth 0. Centre-event time shift <= 1.24 s, interval metrics <= 0.00013 pct-pt, hourly-sample metrics <= 0.0 pct-pt. Position effect (<= 0.53 m on the DEM) is not covered by this angle bound.

Site is the published product-78 ROI3 centroid (PGDA product 78 ROI shapefile (Barker et al. 2021), polygon-vertex centroid, fetched 2026-11-14 (fetch_extra_nasa_data.sh, SHA-256 pinned)), 1510.6 m from the tile centre. Local slope at the point (5 m DEM, 50 m baseline) = 21.4 deg.

site.coordinates_source: PGDA product 78 ROI shapefile (Barker et al. 2021), polygon-vertex centroid, fetched 2026-11-14 (fetch_extra_nasa_data.sh, SHA-256 pinned); SOURCE-BASED UNVALIDATED

frame.body_fixed_frame: DEMs: MOON_ME (DE421) per PGDA README; Horizons: MEAN_ME high precision (DE441). Offset not applied; bounded by science/frame_tie.py (see validation_status).
frame.grid_to_local: at longitude L: local north = (sin L, cos L), local east = (cos L, -sin L) in grid (x, y); grid_az = local_az + L
frame.local_enu: e = d/dlon, n = d/dlat, u = radial unit vector of the site
frame.azimuth: degrees clockwise from LOCAL north (0 N, 90 E); identical to JPL Horizons surface-observer azimuth
frame.elevation: degrees above the plane normal to the site radius vector; airless (no refraction)
frame.model_3d: P = (R + h) * [cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat]; el = asin((P - P_obs).u / |P - P_obs|)

datum.heights: metres above the 1737.4 km reference sphere (LOLA LDEM convention)

time.no_extrapolation: samples and events are only at Horizons-evaluated times

flat_baseline.note: Flat-horizon control: mathematical horizon (0 deg) for every bin; smooth_sphere_dip_deg is the bare-sphere geometric dip at this observer height.

skyline.method: great-circle rays, closed-form polar stereographic, bilinear DEM, Moon-fixed 3D elevation vs local up, single ray per bin centre, no refraction

sources.description: LOLA LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ.TIF, 80 m/px south-polar mosaic, PGDA product 90
JPL Horizons API, observer tables, CENTER=coord@301, QUANTITIES=4,13,20, APPARENT=AIRLESS
LOLA site04_roi3 5 m LDEM (Barker et al. 2021), PGDA product 78

limitations: Local geometric terrain visibility only; not certified illumination/power or DSN telecom availability.
Single ray per 0.5 deg azimuth bin at the bin centre; sub-bin peaks can be missed.
Near field 5 m to the inscribed radius of the product-78 tile, far field 80 m to max_range_m; DEM interpolation is bilinear.
Skyline bins with status "truncated" are lower bounds; "range_limited" bins could be raised by terrain beyond max_range_m.
Visible-disk fraction treats the local skyline as a straight line across the disk (slope from adjacent bins); no limb darkening.
Horizons observer altitude uses DEM height without the mast (sub-mm parallax effect).
DE421 MOON_ME (DEM) vs Horizons MEAN_ME (DE441) frame offset is not applied; ROI bundles bound its effect (<= 1.8e-5 deg, ~0.53 m, NAIF moon_de440_220930.tf) in validation_status.

Tile-centre bundles (site01, site04) use archived app coordinates; ROI bundles use product-78 ROI centroids, and a centroid is a single representative point of a polygon, not a surveyed landing point.
